# Honglin Li

> I am an energy systems researcher and a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Kansas State University. I build optimization and techno-economic models that show which low-carbon technology mixes deliver reliable, affordable energy, and who pays for them. My doctoral research asked when flexibility, from hydrogen or from demand, adds value to a low-carbon energy system, at the scale of a plant, a state and the U.S. nuclear fleet. My current research asks how large new electricity loads such as AI data centers can be supplied with firm, low-carbon power, including small modular reactors.

## Frameworks

- [Nuclear–hydrogen integration framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/nuclear-hydrogen-integration): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [SMR cogeneration framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/smr-datacenter-cogeneration): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [CoDE framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/code-delayed-energization): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [TXH2 framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/txh2-ercot-hydrogen): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [REopt hydrogen framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/reopt-hydrogen-framework): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [GHG load-regulation framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/ghg-load-regulation): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [Supply chains with on-site microgrids](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/supply-chain-microgrid-models): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [Wind UQ surrogate framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/wind-uq-surrogate): Python model framework; MIT code license.
- [MF-GPR framework](https://github.com/Henryutd2021/mfgpr-wind-power-curve): Python model framework; MIT code license.
